title: Nonce-priming KV probing — integration notes and rollout checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a lightweight design and integration checklist for a tentative technique we're calling "nonce-priming" — a targeted, short-prefix speculative probe that warms KV caches and exercises alternate kernel paths without committing to generated tokens returned to the client. The goal is to reduce cold-KV misses and let the scheduler pick better kernel variant & placement for the real request while bounding extra compute and privacy surface.

Background and motivation:
- Problem: cold KV cache misses and suboptimal kernel selection cause tail latencies and token-cost variance for short-to-medium sequences (typical chat turns 8–64 tokens).
- Existing approaches: early-token prefetching and speculative decode variants are in flight, but we need a low-risk model-integration plan to make a conservative probe that can be A/Bed, measured, and rolled back safely.
- Nonce-priming concept: for an incoming request, the runtime issues 1–3 lightweight speculative micro-requests (the "probes") that compute KV state and generate traces but do not count against user-visible output. The probes are tagged with a one-time nonce and executed on a small fast path (short sequence, minimal sampling diversity).

Design constraints and invariants:
1) Privacy and determinism:
   - Probe outputs must never be exposed to clients or logs that are considered user-facing.
   - Every probe execution is tagged with a single-use nonce to avoid accidental reuse or caching of probe outputs for other customers.
2) Bounded overhead:
   - Probes should target < 12% extra GPU cycles on median requests for the tested workload; goal 5–8% for production targets.
   - Upper bound on extra tokens per request: 1–3 probe tokens (configurable per route).
3) Cache effectivity:
   - Probes must populate the same KV layout as a real decode would for the given prefix length (attention states, cached key/value shards).
4) Kernel probing:
   - Probe runs should exercise candidate kernel paths (FP16/INT8/quant variants) but avoid wide sampling that increases nondeterminism.

Probe lifecycle and tagging:
- Probe nonce: short random string (8 chars) included in internal metadata only.
- Probe TTL: probes expire after being associated with the request; do not persist beyond request lifetime.
- Telemetry tags: route, model-id, kernel-candidate, probe-length, probe-latency, probe-kv-hit-ratio.

Scheduler interaction and decision flow:
1) On receipt of request R: evaluate funnel rules (route, priority, sequence-length distribution).
2) If route opts into nonce-priming and rolling budget available, schedule up to N probes (default N=1) on the lowest-latency compatible device.
3) Collect probe results (kv-population-metrics, kernel-performance hints) asynchronously but within request budget window (e.g., 40ms for probes on low-latency routes).
4) Use probe signals to select kernel variant and node placement for the live decode; a negative signal (no improvement) should not block serving — fallback to conservative selection.

Kernel contract and constraints (what probes must reveal):
- Per-token kernel throughput as micro-benchmarked for the probe sequence length.
- Observed KV cache hit counts (per-shard where applicable) and expected prefetch utility.
- Memory pressure signals (peak vram during probe, projected next-token footprint).
- Quantization compatibility flag (if probe fails on INT8 variant, mark as incompatible for this request).

KV cache considerations:
- Probe must write the same kv-encoding layer that live decodes use. For sharded KV stores, probe should target the same shard subset using the request routing key.
- Since probes are nonce-tagged, caching layers that deduplicate prefixes across requests must skip dedup for probes (to avoid cross-request leakage).
- Probe writes are ephemeral: mark as "warming-only" so they do not increment global cache weights or eviction counters.

Acceptance criteria (for enabling on a route):
- Latency: p99 end-to-end serving latency improves or remains equal within 2% vs baseline on experiments where probes choose alternate kernels; p50 and p95 are expected to improve.
- Cost: 95th-percentile token-equivalent GPU time increase is <6% with median <3%.
- Quality/regression: outputs (for deterministic tests) must be bit-identical to baseline when probes are disabled; when probes change kernel selection, quality regression must be within defined eval thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-quality metrics depending on route).
- Safety: no probe has produced user-visible tokens or persisted probe-specific model outputs in customer logs in the experiment run.

Rollback plan (fast and safe):
1) Feature flag off: disable nonce-priming traffic at routing level — this must be <1s toggle for Hosted and Dedicated control planes.
2) For Private deployments: provide a config toggle that sets probes-per-request to 0 and a runtime flag that prevents probe scheduling.
3) Hotfix rollback: if a problematic kernel variant is selected as a result of probes, have an override blacklist keyed by model-id+kernel-id that forces fallback to conservative kernel.
4) Postmortem instrumentation: collect all probe traces, kernel selection changes, and a subset of full request traces for the incident window.

Metrics and instrumentation (what we will record):
- probe.count (per-route, per-model)
- probe.latency_ms (histogram)
- probe.kv_populated_keys (gauge)
- kernel.switches_due_to_probe (counter)
- probe-induced_gpu_ms (estimate)
- request.latency_before_kernel_select and request.latency_after_kernel_select (for causal attribution)
- regressions.detected_by_eval_suite (counter)
- probe.privacy_checks_passed (boolean gauge per-run)

Experiment matrix and test harness:
- A/B test groups: baseline (no probing), probe-enabled (N=1), probe-aggressive (N=2, longer prefixes)
- Traffic slice: start with internal-only (10% traffic on staging), then canary 1% production, then 10%, 33%, 100% based on thresholds.
- Workloads: short-chat (8–24 tokens), medium-chat (24–64), long-context (>256) — probe heuristics should degrade gracefully for long contexts (disable probes for >512 tokens by default).
- Deterministic test suite: run the eval suite with probe toggle forced on/off to detect output deltas.

Operational checklist before enabling route-level rollout:
- [ ] Kernel telemetry: encourage kernel authors to add debug-only counters for probe runs.
- [ ] QA harness: automated regression suite covering top-50 user prompts for the route.
- [ ] Budgeting: set global probe budget to <10% of GPU cycles for first 30 days.
- [ ] Alerts: create SLO-linked alerts for p99 latency regression >5% and cost increase threshold crossing.
- [ ] Privacy review: approvals from security/compliance for ephemeral writes and internal metadata tagging.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: probes cause cache thrash when many concurrent requests probe different prefixes -> Mitigation: add adaptive backoff per-shard and per-route probe suppression when kv eviction rate spikes.
- Risk: probes accidentally persist or leak -> Mitigation: enforce write-mode flags at store-level to discard probe writes on persistent KV backends.
- Risk: probes bias scheduler toward heavier kernels that hurt multi-tenant throughput -> Mitigation: normalize kernel signals by device utilization and weight by historical fairness metrics.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How should probes behave for streaming responses? (Suggestion: run probes only on first chunk and skip for streaming low-latency flows.)
- Should probes be allowed to hit fallback models (smaller quantized variants) to favor cost-reduction hints? If so, how do we ensure comparability?
- Can we instrument a simulated probe-only run on historical traces to estimate global benefit without running live probes? (Action: Samir to prototype replay harness.)

Next steps and ownership:
- Samir P: prototype probe scheduler + nonce tagging (ETA 3 weeks) — PRs: github.com/redwood/serve/pull/2187
- Lina M: add probe metrics to observability dashboards and SLOs (ETA 2 weeks)
- Noah R: experiment harness and deterministic regression pipelines (ETA 4 weeks)
- Priya K: coordinate privacy review and draft short compliance guidance (ETA 1 week)

Appendix: minimal probe config knobs (internal names)
- probe.enabled: boolean per-route
- probe.max_prefix_tokens: integer (default 2)
- probe.max_parallel: integer (default 1)
- probe.latency_budget_ms: integer (default 40)
- probe.ephemeral_write: boolean (always true in design)

Short rationale summary for exec: nonce-priming is a low-friction speculative warm-up that aims to reduce tail latency by informing kernel selection and warming local KV. It is designed to be reversible, auditable, and low-cost, and should be validated through staged experiments with clear rollback and telemetry.
